title: Concise LLM Adapters Playbook — Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP & CLI microexamples
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Produce a compact, opinionated playbook that demonstrates how to integrate Redwood Inference SDKs across three platforms (Next.js edge/SSR, FastAPI backend, Go HTTP server) plus a tiny CLI example. Each microexample focuses on: 1) ergonomic streaming (server + client patterns), 2) robust retry/backoff strategies with idempotency keys, 3) context/cancellation handling for latency SLOs, and 4) minimal production hardening (metrics, tracing hooks, and sensible timeouts). Deliverables: - Next.js example: two variants (edge function streaming + API route server-side streaming) with token-level progress UI and reconnect pattern. - FastAPI example: async generator endpoint with chunked responses, per-request KV cache hints, and retry wrapper util for transient 5xx/429s. - Go HTTP server: context-aware handler with graceful shutdown, exponential backoff middleware, and a small concurrency limiter tailored to Dedicated capacity semantics. - CLI: compact Go/Python CLI that showcases streaming output with a progress bar and safe abort semantics. - Cookbook snippets: copy-paste-ready patterns for backoff configs (jittered/backoff ceilings), streaming buffer sizes, and batching knobs for low-latency conversational flows. Success criteria: working sample repos + README, CI smoke test that validates streaming and retry behaviors, docs page in the SDK Playbooks section, and a short demo recording for onboarding. Links: PRD: https://confluence.company/reddoc/sdk-playbooks-llm-adapters (draft), GitHub draft repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-playbooks/pull/527 (WIP), demo checklist: https://docs.redwood/demo-checklists/sdk-playbooks. Note: keep examples intentionally minimal (<=200 LOC per sample) so they are easy to copy into customer apps.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Kickoff: scoped to 4 microexamples. Decided on Next.js (edge + API route), FastAPI async generator, Go net/http with context, and a single-file CLI in Python. Referenced earlier starter guides but kept names/patterns different to avoid overlap.

2026-02-17 - Design review with DX: agreed on token-progress UI for Next.js and a simple reconnection token pattern rather than complex websockets to keep examples deployable on Vercel. Action: Marco to prototype edge streaming shim.

2026-02-22 - Engineering sync: chose retry defaults: base=100ms, max=4s, factor=2.0, full jitter. Use idempotency keys on non-streaming requests; recommend 'prefer-not-to-retry' for streaming partials (document tradeoffs).

2026-03-02 - Prototype PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-playbooks/pull/527. FastAPI sample demonstrates async generator with try/except around Redwood client iteration to surface errors to monitoring. Requesting review from @Lena Ortiz and @Samir Rao.
2026-03-05 - Code review feedback from Lena: add a small integration test that asserts client cancellation stops server-side generation within 250ms. Marco to add test and CI job (smoke-stream).

2026-03-08 - Decision: Go example will include a lightweight semaphore-based concurrency limiter instead of a full rate limiter to keep scope small. Document when to migrate to a token-bucket approach for Dedicated clusters.

2026-03-10 - UX feedback: examples should expose explicit knobs for batching/window sizes. Added snippet table in README recommending ranges (window_tokens: 16-128, batch_size: 4-32) and explanation for latency vs cost trade-off.

2026-03-12 - Updated demos: added trace hooks to all samples (opentelemetry link in README) and recorded a 3-minute walkthrough video (internal link: https://drive.company/redwood/sdk-playbooks-walkthrough.mp4). Next step: add CI flakiness guard and finalize docs page.
